name: Antrea bast fishing net
description: A willow-bast fishing net from Antrea preserves evidence of knotted mesh. A comparative analysis identified its illustrated netting knot as a form of the sheet bend.

impact.note: One preserved net witnessing mesh fishing, which was already older; nothing is known to rest on this object.

date.label: 8400–8300 calibrated BCE
date.basis: Approximate date reported by Mäkelä and Kunnas and Bender Jørgensen et al. Other published age estimates or site-level calibrations use different samples or treatments.

events.statement: The surviving Antrea fishing net is made of knotted willow-bast cordage. Its published knot drawing was identified as a form of sheet bend.

evidence.supports: Fishing net remains of willow bast, with other objects, are dated to 8400–8300 calibrated BCE; the suggested boat context is an interpretation.
The authors report a willow-bast fishing net with knots, floats and sinkers dated 8400–8300 cal BC at Antrea in present-day Russia.

evidence.locator: pp. 479–481, Discussion: Cultural transmission, task differentiation, and the deep past of knots; Fig. 1E
evidence.supports: Reanalyses the published Antrea knot and identifies it as the sheet-bend form shown in Figure 1E. The analysis compares other sites and leaves transfer versus convergence open.

events.caveats: This find witnesses mesh fishing. Boat loss is an interpretation. A reanalysis of the published knot drawing identifies the structure; historical transmission to later nets remains open.

earliest_record.rationale: Date of the supported scoped case; no global priority is implied.

unresolved.note: Recheck the original reporting for Antrea net bast and the bark float dates separately. Kaaronen et al. cite a different age via the Manninen site chronology.
